theory.intro: When $X$ is replaced by $aX+b$, the mean changes in the same way: $E(aX+b)=aE(X)+b$.
facts: $E(aX+b)=aE(X)+b$: multiply the mean by $a$, then add $b$.
Adding $b$ shifts every value equally, so it moves the centre.
This rule needs only $E(X)$, not the whole distribution.
steps: Write the new variable in the form $aX+b$ and read off $a$ and $b$.

foundation.question_text:
Raw test marks $X$ have mean $58$.
The marks are scaled using $Y=1.2X+5$.
Find the mean scaled mark.

development.question_text:
The daily maximum temperature $X$, in degrees Celsius, has $E(X)=21.5$.
The temperature in degrees Fahrenheit is $F=1.8X+32$.
Find $E(F)$.

A worker's weekly overtime hours $H$ have $E(H)=4.2$.
Weekly pay in dollars is $W=920+45H$.
Find $E(W)$, correct to the nearest cent.

mastery.question_text:
The random variable $X$ has the distribution below.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & 1 & 2 & 4 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.3 & 0.5 & 0.2 \end{array}$
Find $E(3X-5)$.

The random variable $X$ has the distribution below.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} x & -2 & 0 & 3 & 5 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.2 & 0.3 & 0.4 & 0.1 \end{array}$
Find $E(2.5X-1.8)$.

A game's net gain $X$ in dollars has $E(X)=-0.5$.
The operator triples the player's net gain and then charges an extra $\$1$, so the new net gain is $Y=3X-1$.
Find $E(Y)$, and state whether the change helps the player.
mastery.solution_text:
$E(Y)=3(-0.5)-1$
$=-1.5-1$
$=-\$2.50$
The expected loss per play grows from $\$0.50$ to $\$2.50$, so the change does not help the player.
